description:
Execute shell commands on a Linux environment. The host OS, shell, and terminal backend are stated in your environment section — write commands for THAT platform. The working directory, files and exported variables persist between calls: activate a virtualenv or export once, not before every command.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail (use read_file), grep/rg/find/ls (use search_files), sed/awk (use patch), or echo/heredoc file creation (use write_file). Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers — anything that needs a shell. Output is auto-truncated with the full text saved to a file — never pipe through tail/head to shorten it.
Foreground (default): returns INSTANTLY when the command finishes, even with a high timeout — set timeout generously for long builds and fixed waits.
Background: set background=true (returns a session_id) only for commands that must keep running independently after this tool call returns; add notify=true for bounded tasks, leave silent only for servers/daemons that never exit. Do not start sleep, timers, cooldowns, delays, or polling loops with background=true — to wait a fixed time, run the wait as a normal foreground command with a high enough timeout. After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check in a separate call (no blind sleep loops); manage with process_manage(action="poll"/"wait").
Working directory: use 'workdir' for per-command cwd; when a command changes the session cwd (cd, pushd), trust the result's "cwd" field instead of prefixing every command with 'cd'.
PTY: pty=true + background=true for interactive CLIs (they hang without a terminal); drive them with process_manage write/submit. Local backend only. Pipe git output to cat if it might page.
Persist: background=true, persist_on_release=true keeps the job alive across agent lifecycle cleanup (session end, /new, compression, error recovery, stop-on-max-iterations). Use ONLY for long-running jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation; the user can still stop it on purpose.
name: terminal

background.description: Keep running after this call returns; returns a session_id.

command.description: The shell command to execute. Optional when mode='interactive' (defaults to a persistent shell session).

heartbeat.description: With background=true: also notify every N seconds (min 60) with new output; quiet ticks are skipped. For bounded jobs you must react to mid-run, never servers. Implies notify=true; 0 = off.

inactivity_timeout.description: Seconds of output silence before a wait returns early with partial output (process_id continuation waits; default 120 when wait_for_pattern is set).

interactive.description: Start a persistent interactive shell/REPL (local backend, PTY). Equivalent to mode='interactive'. Continue it later with terminal(command=..., process_id=<session_id>).

mode.description: Execution mode: 'run'/'execute'/'foreground' (default, blocks until done), 'background' (== background=true, returns a session_id), 'interactive' (start a persistent shell/REPL session you continue later via process_id). Overrides `background` when set.

notify.description: With background=true. true: one notification on exit; use it for anything that ends (builds, tests, deploys), or the job runs silently. ['pattern', ...]: notify when a line matches, only for one-shot readiness on processes that never exit; rate-limited. Omit for servers/daemons.

persist_on_release.description: With background=true: survive session end, /new, compression and other cleanup (not host exit). Only for jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation.

process_id.description: Continue an existing background process (session_id from terminal background or process(action='list')): send `command` to its stdin and wait for its NEW output (kimi-style session continuation). Requires the process to accept stdin (PTY/pipe).

promote_on_timeout.description: Foreground only (local backend): if the command exceeds `timeout`, DON'T kill it — keep it running and return a background session_id you can poll/wait/log/kill. Long work is never lost. Also enables wait_for_pattern early-return.

pty.description: With background=true: pseudo-terminal for interactive CLIs (REPLs, coding agents); drive it with process_manage write/submit. Local backend only.

timeout.description: Max seconds (default 180, foreground max 600). Finishing early returns at once, so set it generously. Above 600s the command runs as a tracked background process with notify_on_complete=true (the result says so; do not re-run it).

wait_for_pattern.description: Regex. With promote_on_timeout=true (foreground): return as soon as it appears in output; the process keeps running as a background session. With process_id (continuation): wait for new output matching this regex. Use for server-readiness signals instead of polling.

workdir.description: Absolute working directory for this command only.
